questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Indus Valley site is famous for the Great Bath?
questions.explanation: The Great Bath, a large public water tank, was discovered at Mohenjo-daro, indicating advanced water management and ritualistic practices.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Where was the First Buddhist Council held?
questions.explanation: The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajgir shortly after the Buddha's death under the patronage of King Ajatashatru.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the founder of the Maurya Empire?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda dynasty and established the Maurya Empire with the help of Chanakya.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Mughal emperor introduced the syncretic religion ?Din-i-Ilahi??
questions.explanation: Akbar founded Din-i-Ilahi in 1582, combining elements of various religions, to promote religious harmony.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Revolt of 1857 began at which military station?
questions.explanation: The revolt broke out on 10 May 1857 at Meerut when Indian sepoys refused to use greased cartridges, leading to the First War of Independence.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which is the oldest Veda among the four Vedas?
questions.explanation: Rigveda is the oldest Veda, composed around 1500?1200 BCE, consisting of hymns in praise of various deities.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which Gupta ruler is known as the ?Napoleon of India??
questions.explanation: Samudragupta is called the 'Napoleon of India' due to his extensive military conquests across the Indian subcontinent.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who was the founder of the Maratha Empire?
questions.explanation: Shivaji founded the Maratha Empire in the 17th century and was crowned as Chhatrapati in 1674.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler issued the 'Edicts of Ashoka' primarily to spread the principles of Dhamma among the people?
questions.explanation: Emperor Ashoka, after the devastating Kalinga War (261 BCE), embraced Buddhism and propagated the principles of Dhamma through a series of rock and pillar edicts across his empire.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: The 'Mansabdari system', which was a rank-based administrative and military system, was introduced during the reign of which Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: The Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar around 1571 CE. Under this system, every officer of the state was assigned a rank (mansab) that determined his salary and the number of cavalry he was required to maintain.

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to freedom of religion?
questions.explanation: Article 25 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, and health. Articles 25 to 28 together deal with the Right to Freedom of Religion.

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question: By which Constitutional Amendment Act were the Fundamental Duties added to the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976, enacted during the Emergency period, added Part IV-A (Article 51-A) containing 10 Fundamental Duties to the Constitution, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha, as prescribed by the Constitution of India, is ?
questions.explanation: Article 80 of the Constitution prescribes that the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha shall not exceed 250 ? up to 238 elected representatives of States and Union Territories, plus 12 members nominated by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution contains the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in Part IV of the Constitution (Articles 36 to 51). These are non-justiciable guidelines for the State in making laws and policies for social and economic welfare.

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can the President declare a Financial Emergency?
questions.explanation: Article 360 of the Constitution empowers the President to proclaim a Financial Emergency if the financial stability or credit of India or any part thereof is threatened. So far, no Financial Emergency has been declared in India.

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Right to Equality guaranteed to citizens?
questions.explanation: Article 14 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Equality, stating that the State shall not deny to any person equality before law or equal protection of the laws within India.

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question: In which Part of the Indian Constitution are the Directive Principles of State Policy contained?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in Part IV (Articles 36?51) of the Indian Constitution. They are inspired by the Irish Constitution and are non-justiciable in nature.

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding a Joint Sitting of the two Houses of Parliament in India is correct?
options: It is presided over by the President of India
It is presided over by the Speaker of Lok Sabha
It is presided over by the Chairman of Rajya Sabha
It can be convened for any type of Bill
questions.explanation: Under Article 108, a Joint Sitting of both Houses is presided over by the Speaker of Lok Sabha (or the Deputy Speaker in his absence). It can only be convened for ordinary Bills, not for Money Bills or Constitution Amendment Bills.

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976, often called the 'Mini Constitution', inserted the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' into the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Polity & Constitution
questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution: (1) It can be proclaimed on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. (2) It must be approved by each House of Parliament by a simple majority within one month. (3) Once approved, it continues for a period of six months unless revoked earlier. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (1) is correct ? Article 352 allows proclamation on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. Statement (3) is correct ? once approved by Parliament it continues for six months unless revoked. Statement (2) is incorrect because Parliament must approve it by a special majority (two-thirds of members present and voting, which must also be a majority of the total membership of each House), not a simple majority.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to the frequent floods it causes in the state?
questions.explanation: The Kosi river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because it frequently changes its course and causes devastating floods in the plains of Bihar every year.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which type of soil is most suitable for cotton cultivation and is predominantly found in the Deccan Plateau region?
questions.explanation: Black soil (also called Regur or Black Cotton Soil) is rich in clay minerals and has high moisture retention capacity, making it ideal for cotton cultivation. It is mainly found in the Deccan Plateau, covering Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The South-West Monsoon normally arrives at the coast of Kerala by which approximate date every year?
questions.explanation: The South-West Monsoon normally arrives at the Kerala coast around 1st June each year, marking the official onset of the monsoon season in India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which mountain pass connects the Leh region of Ladakh with the Manali region of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Baralacha La (also spelled Bara-lacha La) is the high-altitude mountain pass that lies on the Leh-Manali Highway, connecting the Leh district of Ladakh with Manali in Himachal Pradesh.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which type of natural vegetation is typically found in areas of India that receive an annual rainfall between 50 cm and 100 cm?
questions.explanation: Tropical Deciduous Forests (also called Monsoon Forests) are found in regions receiving annual rainfall between 70 cm and 200 cm, with the dry deciduous variety common between 50 cm and 100 cm. These forests shed their leaves in the dry season and are the most widespread forest type in India.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which Five Year Plan in India gave the highest priority to the reduction of economic inequalities and poverty alleviation for the first time as its central objective?
questions.explanation: The Fifth Five Year Plan (1974?79) was the first to explicitly place poverty eradication (Garibi Hatao) and reduction of inequalities at the core of its objectives, also introducing the Minimum Needs Programme.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: The concept of 'Priority Sector Lending' in India requires commercial banks to mandatorily lend a fixed percentage of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) to specified sectors. What is the prescribed overall target for domestic scheduled commercial banks?
questions.explanation: As per RBI guidelines, domestic scheduled commercial banks are required to lend 40% of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) to priority sectors such as agriculture, MSMEs, education, housing, and weaker sections.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the difference between GDP at Market Price and GDP at Factor Cost?
options: GDP at MP = GDP at FC + Subsidies - Indirect Taxes
GDP at MP = GDP at FC + Indirect Taxes - Subsidies
GDP at MP = GDP at FC - Indirect Taxes - Subsidies
GDP at MP = GDP at FC + Direct Taxes - Subsidies
questions.explanation: GDP at Market Price = GDP at Factor Cost + Indirect Taxes - Subsidies. Market prices include indirect taxes paid by consumers but exclude subsidies provided by the government, so net indirect taxes (Indirect Taxes minus Subsidies) are added to factor cost.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: The term 'Operation Flood', launched in 1970 in India, is associated with which of the following sectors?
questions.explanation: Operation Flood, launched in 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) under Dr. Verghese Kurien, was the world's largest dairy development programme and is credited with making India the world's largest milk producer ? an achievement known as the White Revolution.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: The New Economic Policy of 1991 in India was introduced during the tenure of which Finance Minister?
questions.explanation: The New Economic Policy of 1991, built on the pillars of Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation (LPG), was introduced by Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh in the Union Budget of 1991 under Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao's government.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which part of the human brain is primarily responsible for maintaining body balance and coordination of muscular movements?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum, located at the rear of the brain, coordinates voluntary muscle movements and is responsible for maintaining posture and balance.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following substances turns red litmus paper blue, indicating its basic nature?
questions.explanation: Baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) is alkaline in nature and turns red litmus paper blue, whereas vinegar, lemon juice, and tamarind juice are all acidic.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A person suffering from myopia (short-sightedness) cannot see distant objects clearly. Which type of lens is used to correct this defect?
questions.explanation: In myopia, the image forms in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens is used to diverge the incoming light rays so that the image falls correctly on the retina.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Deficiency of which vitamin causes the disease 'Scurvy', characterised by bleeding gums and weakness?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid). It leads to symptoms such as bleeding gums, skin rashes, and general weakness. Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A box of mass 10 kg is lifted vertically through a height of 5 metres. If acceleration due to gravity is 10 m/s?, what is the work done against gravity?
questions.explanation: Work done = mass ? gravitational acceleration ? height = 10 ? 10 ? 5 = 500 J. This equals the gravitational potential energy gained by the box.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A shopkeeper marks the price of an article 40% above its cost price and then gives a discount of 20% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become 5 times itself at the same rate of interest?
questions.explanation: If principal doubles in 8 years, interest earned = P in 8 years, so rate R = 100/(8) = 12.5% per year. To become 5 times, interest needed = 4P. Time = (4P ? 100)/(P ? 12.5) = 32 years.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5. If 6 is added to each number, the new ratio becomes 3 : 4. What is the smaller of the two original numbers?
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be 3k and 5k. Then (3k+6)/(5k+6) = 3/4. Cross-multiplying: 12k+24 = 15k+18, so 3k = 6, k = 2. Smaller number = 3?2 = 6.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A alone can complete a work in 24 days and B alone in 16 days. They work together for 6 days, after which A leaves. In how many days will B complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation: A's 1-day work = 1/24, B's 1-day work = 1/16. Together per day = 1/24 + 1/16 = (2+3)/48 = 5/48. In 6 days, work done = 6 ? 5/48 = 30/48 = 5/8. Remaining work = 1 - 5/8 = 3/8. Time taken by B = (3/8) ? (1/16) = (3/8) ? 16 = 6 days.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: The average of 5 consecutive even numbers is 34. What is the largest of these 5 numbers?
questions.explanation: For consecutive even numbers, the average equals the middle (3rd) number. So the 3rd number = 34. The 5 numbers are 30, 32, 34, 36, 38. The largest is 38.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: Which type of Sandhi is formed in the word '?????' (sajjan)?
questions.explanation: ?????' is formed from '???' + '??'. Here the consonant '??' meets '??', resulting in '???', which is an example of Vyanjan Sandhi (consonant junction).

questions.question: What is the correct meaning of the idiom '????? ??????'?
questions.explanation: The idiom '????? ??????' means to avoid someone's gaze or to stay out of sight, typically out of guilt or embarrassment.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: What is the correct antonym of the word '????'?
questions.explanation: ????' means to take or receive, and its antonym is '??????', which means to give or bestow. The compound phrase '????-??????' itself means exchange.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: Which type of Samas (compound) is formed in the word '????????'?
questions.explanation: ????????' means 'according to one's ability' (????? ?? ??????). When the first element is an indeclinable word (?????) like '???' and gives the compound an adverbial meaning, it is called Avyayibhav Samas.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: Identify the correct sentence among the following:
questions.explanation: The grammatically correct sentence is '???? ???? ????? ?? ??? ???' Here '?????' is feminine, so the verb form '?? ??? ??' is correct. Option C uses '?????' which is wrong with the verb '????', and Option D uses masculine verb '???' incorrectly with a feminine subject.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'OBSTINATE'.
questions.explanation: Obstinate' means refusing to change one's opinion or course of action despite pressure, which is closest in meaning to 'Stubborn'. The other options convey unrelated or opposite traits.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to 'FRUGAL'.
questions.explanation: Frugal' means economical and avoiding waste, so its antonym is 'Extravagant', which means spending money excessively or wastefully. 'Thrifty' is actually a synonym of frugal.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate preposition to fill in the blank: She has been waiting _____ two hours for the bus.
questions.explanation: For' is used with a period or duration of time (e.g., two hours, three days). 'Since' is used with a specific point in time (e.g., Monday, morning). Since 'two hours' is a duration, 'for' is correct.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for: 'A person who is unable to pay their debts'.
questions.explanation: Insolvent' specifically refers to a person or organisation that is unable to pay their debts. The other options refer to entirely different concepts unrelated to financial inability.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error: (A) The committee / (B) have taken / (C) its decision / (D) unanimously.
questions.explanation: Committee' is a collective noun and in formal/standard British and American grammar it is treated as singular when acting as a single unit, so the correct verb form is 'has taken', not 'have taken'.

questions.subject: Reasoning/Analytical Ability
questions.question: Find the missing number in the series: 4, 9, 20, 43, 90, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern is: each term is multiplied by 2 and then 1 is added. 4?2+1=9, 9?2+2=20, 20?2+3=43, 43?2+4=90, 90?2+3=183. More precisely the rule is ?2 then add 1, 2, 3, 4, 3... Let us re-check: 4?2+1=9 ?, 9?2+2=20 ?, 20?2+3=43 ?, 43?2+4=90 ?, 90?2+3=183 ?. The correct answer is 183.

questions.subject: Reasoning/Analytical Ability
questions.question: In a certain code language, 'RIVER' is written as 'SJWFS'. Using the same rule, how will 'CLOUD' be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter in the word is shifted one place forward in the alphabet: R+1=S, I+1=J, V+1=W, E+1=F, R+1=S, giving SJWFS. Applying the same rule to CLOUD: C+1=D, L+1=M, O+1=P, U+1=V, D+1=E ? DMPVE.

questions.subject: Reasoning/Analytical Ability
questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, Meena says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my father.' How is Meena related to the person in the photograph?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of Meena's father is Meena herself. So the mother of the person in the photograph is Meena, meaning Meena is his/her Mother.

questions.subject: Reasoning/Analytical Ability
questions.question: Rahul starts from point A and walks 8 km towards the North, then turns right and walks 6 km, then turns right again and walks 8 km. How far is he from point A, and in which direction?
questions.explanation: Rahul goes 8 km North, then 6 km East (right turn), then 8 km South (right turn). He is now at the same North-South level as A but 6 km to the East of A. So he is 6 km East of point A.

questions.subject: Reasoning/Analytical Ability
questions.question: Statements: All pens are books. Some books are copies. Conclusions: I. Some pens are copies. II. Some copies are books. Which of the following is correct?
options: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: From 'All pens are books' and 'Some books are copies', we cannot directly conclude that some pens are copies (the books that are copies may not include any pen). However, 'Some books are copies' directly implies 'Some copies are books' by conversion. So only Conclusion II follows.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which city has been identified as the proposed host for India's bid to host the 2036 Summer Olympics?
questions.explanation: The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) is pursuing India's bid to host the 2036 Summer Olympics, with Ahmedabad identified as the proposed host city. India formally submitted its Letter of Intent to the IOC's Future Host Commission in October 2024.[reference:0]

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which country became a permanent member of the G20 during India's presidency?
questions.explanation: In a major diplomatic victory under India's G20 presidency, the African Union became a permanent member of the grouping.[reference:2]

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Who is the current Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (as of August 2026)?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Malhotra is the current Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (as of August 2026). He addressed the FIBAC 2026 conference and announced key policy decisions.[reference:4][reference:5]

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: NASA invited ISRO to join which space programme in August 2026?
options: Moon Base Programme under Artemis Accords
questions.explanation: NASA invited the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) to join its Moon Base programme under the Artemis Accords, deepening the U.S.-India deep space partnership.[reference:8][reference:9]

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: What was the GDP growth projection for 2026-27 as announced by the RBI Governor in August 2026?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India projected real GDP growth at 6.7 per cent for 2026-27, while keeping the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 percent.[reference:12][reference:13]

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which two Bills were passed by the Lok Sabha in a span of 14 minutes in August 2026?
options: Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 and National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026
Farm Bills 2026 and GST Amendment Bill 2026

Anti-Defection Bill 2026 and Electoral Reform Bill 2026

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: In August 2026, which country's Prime Minister had a telephonic conversation with PM Modi, reviewing the India-Israel strategic partnership?
questions.explanation: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke with PM Modi, discussing West Asia and reviewing progress in the India-Israel strategic partnership.[reference:18][reference:19]

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: How many Padma awards were announced for the year 2026?
questions.explanation: The Government of India announced 131 Padma honours for 2026, including five Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri awards.[reference:22][reference:23]

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: In August 2026, India and the US commenced a joint navy exercise in which city?
questions.explanation: On 10 August 2026, the Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) 2026 Exercise began between the Indian Navy and the US Navy in Kochi.[reference:26]

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: What was the theme of the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration adopted unanimously under India's G20 presidency?
options: One Earth, One Family, One Future
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Modi chaired a session on the theme "One Future" on the final day of the G20 Summit, where the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration was unanimously adopted.[reference:28]

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a neighbouring country of India?
questions.explanation: India shares its borders with 7 countries ? Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Afghanistan. Thailand does not share a border with India.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: As per the NIRF Rankings 2025, which institution was ranked as India's best research institute?
questions.explanation: The NIRF Rankings 2025 placed the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru as the country's best research institute, topping the Research Institutions category for the fifth consecutive year (2021?2025).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Repealing and Amending Bill, 2025, passed by the Indian Parliament, repeals how many Acts?
questions.explanation: The Repealing and Amending Bill, 2025, provides for the repeal of 71 Acts, including the Indian Tramways Act, 1886, the Levy Sugar Price Equalisation Fund Act, 1976, and the Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited Act, 1988.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: National Technology Day is observed in India on which date?
questions.explanation: National Technology Day is celebrated annually in India on May 11, commemorating the successful nuclear tests at Pokhran in 1998.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO), founded on April 7, 1948, has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: In September 2025, which region of Himachal Pradesh was officially inscribed as India's first high-altitude Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
questions.explanation: In September 2025, the trans-Himalayan landscape of Lahaul and Spiti was inscribed as India's first high-altitude Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve, spanning approximately 7,770 sq km.

questions.question: Who among the following was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 for the English novel "Crimson Spring"?
questions.explanation: English author and former ambassador Navtej Sarna was named the recipient of the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 for his novel "Crimson Spring".

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), 2025 was India's __________ warmest year on record.
questions.explanation: India recorded its eighth warmest year on record in 2025, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), despite a relatively mild summer and robust monsoon.

It was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, along with Egypt and Mesopotamia. The cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro were well-planned with grid patterns, advanced drainage systems, and standardized burnt brick buildings. The United Nations adopted the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in 2015, which include 17 goals to be achieved by 2030. These goals address issues like poverty, inequality, climate change, and clean energy. Question: How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted by the United Nations?
questions.explanation: The passage states that the SDGs include 17 goals to be achieved by 2030.

questions.subject: Hindi Language
questions.question: Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows: The Indian Constitution, adopted on 26 January 1950, is the supreme law of India. It establishes a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic. The Constitution provides for a parliamentary system of government with a bicameral legislature. Fundamental Rights are guaranteed to all citizens, while Directive Principles of State Policy guide the government in making laws. The Constitution also provides for an independent judiciary with the Supreme Court as the highest court of appeal. Question: When was the Indian Constitution adopted?
questions.explanation: The passage states that the Indian Constitution was adopted on 26 January 1950.

questions.subject: Hindi Language
questions.question: Read the following passage carefully and answer the question that follows: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was established in 1969 to develop India's space program. Its primary objectives include designing and launching satellites for communication, weather forecasting, and navigation. Notable achievements include the Chandrayaan-1 mission, which discovered water on the Moon, the Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM) in 2014, making India the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit, and the Chandrayaan-3 mission, which successfully landed on the Moon's south pole in 2023. Question: In which year was ISRO established?
questions.explanation: The passage states that ISRO was established in 1969.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the Non-Cooperation Movement formally adopted as a resolution?
questions.explanation: The Nagpur Session of the INC in December 1920, presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar, formally adopted the Non-Cooperation Movement resolution moved by Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: Which Indian ruler's adopted son was refused recognition by the British under the Doctrine of Lapse, making Jhansi a direct cause of her joining the Revolt of 1857?
questions.explanation: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi had adopted a son named Damodar Rao after her husband Gangadhar Rao's death, but the British refused to recognize the adoption under the Doctrine of Lapse and annexed Jhansi, which led her to join the 1857 Revolt.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931 led to the suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement. Which of the following was NOT a condition agreed upon in this pact?
options: Permission to make salt on the seacoast for personal use
questions.explanation: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact included release of political prisoners, withdrawal of ordinances, and concessions on salt, but it did NOT grant Purna Swaraj; complete independence was not part of its terms.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885. Who among the following presided over its first session held in Bombay?
questions.explanation: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee (W.C. Bonnerjee) presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress held in Bombay in December 1885, which was organized by A.O. Hume.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: During the Quit India Movement of 1942, which city became famous for the establishment of a parallel government known as the 'Satara Prati Sarkar'?
questions.explanation: During the Quit India Movement, Satara in Maharashtra witnessed the formation of the 'Satara Prati Sarkar' (parallel government), led by Nana Patil, which functioned independently for several years.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Right to Constitutional Remedies guaranteed, which Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 32 grants citizens the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Dr. Ambedkar described it as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution because without it other rights would be meaningless.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: By which Constitutional Amendment were the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens added to the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, inserted Part IV-A containing Article 51-A, which lists the Fundamental Duties of citizens. This was done on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a power exclusively vested in the Rajya Sabha under the Indian Constitution?
options: Passing a resolution under Article 249 to legislate on a State List subject
Passing a resolution under Article 312 to create new All-India Services
Approving the proclamation of Emergency if Lok Sabha is dissolved
questions.explanation: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, never in the Rajya Sabha. The other three options represent special powers that are uniquely or specifically vested in the Rajya Sabha by the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: The concept of a Uniform Civil Code for citizens is contained in which Article of the Indian Constitution under the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.explanation: Article 44 of the Constitution directs the State to endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code for all citizens throughout the territory of India. It falls under Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and added Part IX to the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which came into force in April 1993, gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions by inserting Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) into the Constitution. The 74th Amendment similarly dealt with Urban Local Bodies.
